note: National Park Service campground in an open grass field beside the Current River at the Highway 106 bridge east of Eminence: eight gravel back-in spurs off one gravel drive, four backing toward the river bank. The park calls it a backcountry campground, meaning few amenities; the approach is paved. No drinking water, no trash service. On recreation.gov it is booked under Jacks Fork / Middle Current Backcountry Campsites. Six people per site. Trails lead to Blue Spring and Owls Bend. --Claude
summary: Still a drive-in campground: 8 standard non-electric back-in sites, each listed at 50 ft with RV, trailer and fifth wheel permitted, paved approach, $10 year-round, reservation only on recreation.gov (facility 10344874), vault toilet, no water. Open - all 8 sites bookable in November 2026 and no alert. Stored 'year_round false' and 'max 35 ft' replaced. Riverview stands, with an upgrade lead.
flags: INCLUSION (stays - 'backcountry' is a label, not a walk-in): NPS says 'Within Ozark National Scenic Riverways, a "backcountry campground" refers to campgrounds with some basic amenities, but not as many as developed campgrounds.' For Powder Mill the NPS record gives accessRoads 'Paved Roads - All vehicles OK', rvAllowed 1 ('RVs and trailers are allowed as specified in our campground regulations. Vehicles must not be parked on vegetation.'), classification 'Limited Development Campground', and directions 'After the bridge, take the first right towards the Powder Mill Campground. Drive down the side road until you find a large grass field; this field is the campground.' recreation.gov's eight Powder Mill sites are all Site Access 'Drive-In', Back-in, gravel, Driveway Length 50, RV/Trailer/Fifth Wheel to 50 ft. Imagery shows eight gravel spurs off a gravel drive in a mown field. A 23-ft motorhome fits every site.

OPEN / FLOOD STATUS: no alert names Powder Mill (the four park alerts are Round Spring pavilion lot, 2026 paving at Alley/Round Spring/Pulltite/Big Spring, reservations required, Akers ferry). All eight campsite records are status 'Open', and the November 2026 calendar shows them bookable (174 site-nights Available, 10 Reserved; 56 'Not Reservable', which are past dates). The calendar had no data yet for January 2027 - that is an unreleased window, not a closure.

SEASON CHANGE: stored year_round false with no dates (derived from note prose). The NPS record says 'typically open throughout the year' and the fee page 'Fees apply year-round'. Written year_round true with the flooding caveat.
RIG LENGTH CHANGE: stored max_rig_ft 35 (derived). recreation.gov lists every site at 50 ft for RV, trailer and fifth wheel; the NPS record's rvMaxLength is 0 (blank). Written 50.

WATERFRONT LEAD UP (stored riverview - owner's call): per-site coordinates on leaf-off imagery show sites 1-4 on the river side of the drive, their gravel spurs ending about 25-40 m from the Current River with mown grass and then a single line of bank trees and brush between pad and water - no road, drive or day-use area between. Sites 5-8 are on the far side of the drive, 45-80 m from the water with the drive and the river-side sites between. recreation.gov tags all eight 'Riverfront', but it tags all 52 sites in this facility that way, so that is a type-level label and does not count. The NPS description promises 'lovely views of the Current River'. Riverview is certainly earned; whether four of eight sites behind a bank tree line make it riverfront is the question. I did not change it.

WEBSITE: the stored NPS page is right for information; the booking page is https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/10344874 (written to booking.url). When phoning recreation.gov the park asks callers to name the 'Jacks Fork/Middle Current District' and the campground and site number.
